chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: The fourth string on the bass and Henry Kimball
summary: Whether basses always had a fourth string, and Henry Kimball making Garland put one on and showing him fingering.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Oh yeah. I might give you some change myself. If I can get it. When did the fourth string come in? I wanted to ask you that. Where did you find the fourth string?

Well, as far as I know, they always have fourth strings. They always have? Up to mine. But I used to, most of the boys used to take the E string off. Uh huh. Because the finger though, fourth string, most of the, I was playing, I was playing fourth strings, was, I was playing in the theater and the symphony band. Uh huh. Just like Bowen. They bowed. Yeah. And I was in theater. But the man, because of me playing, using the fourth string, Hendrick Kimball. Oh yeah.
He made me put that string on that bass and he showed me how to finger.
I don't know where he was at that time.
Well he wasn't born then. That's right. He was a youngster. Up in the channel.
He was, he wasn't on his way. He was a youngster.
